Human: Generate a complete medium-size C++17 repository architecture for: Video player.

This architecture will be implemented later by a seeded local code model and evaluated automatically. Produce concrete design and implementation tasks for every file; do not use placeholders.

Normative evaluator protocol (these paths are mandatory and override preferences):
- build file: CMakeLists.txt
- runtime entry: src/Main.cpp
- single test target: tests/test_main.cpp
- test command: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure
- keep exactly one protocol-level test file; additional non-test implementation files are allowed

Language/layout constraints:
Use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. tests/test_main.cpp must include headers, never implementation .cpp files. Use only the C++17 standard library and CMake; do not fetch dependencies. Every header must be self-contained and list every standard-library include needed by its declarations; every source must include algorithms/types it uses.


Project-specific C++ fixed-width integer compilation contract:
- use exactly these files and no substitutes, in dependency order: CMakeLists.txt, include/Time/IClock.h, include/Time/ManualClock.h, include/Time/MonotonicClock.h, include/Media/MediaMetadata.h, include/Playlist/Playlist.h, include/Player/PlaybackState.h, include/Player/Player.h, include/Runtime/App.h, src/Time/ManualClock.cpp, src/Time/MonotonicClock.cpp, src/Media/MediaMetadata.cpp, src/Playlist/Playlist.cpp, src/Player/Player.cpp, src/Runtime/App.cpp, src/Main.cpp, tests/test_main.cpp
- every header that names a signed 64-bit integer must directly contain `#include <cstdint>` and must spell the type `std::int64_t`; bare `int64_t` is forbidden everywhere. In particular include/Time/IClock.h begins its standard-library includes with `#include <cstdint>` before namespace Time and declares `virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0;`
- ManualClock and MonotonicClock override exactly `std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept`; all ManualClock start/delta/current values, MediaMetadata duration values, and Player position/duration/last-time values and parameters use `std::int64_t` consistently in declarations and definitions. Do not mix const/non-const or noexcept/throwing forms across base, derived, header, and source signatures
- tests/test_main.cpp is a self-contained zero-third-party test executable with exactly one `int main()` and ordinary standard-library checks; GoogleTest, Catch2, Boost.Test, doctest, and every other test dependency are forbidden. CMakeLists.txt directly uses `add_executable(video_player_tests tests/test_main.cpp)`, links the project core library, calls `enable_testing()` and `add_test(NAME video_player_tests COMMAND video_player_tests)`, and never uses find_package, FetchContent, ExternalProject, GTest, gtest, or network downloads
- src/Main.cpp contains only a minimal `int main()` that returns `Runtime::App().run_demo()` (or equivalently constructs App then returns run_demo). It never streams or prints PlaybackState or another enum, and contains no interactive or long-running loop
- Full API specification, Logic Analysis, Shared Knowledge, test/build plan, and every affected header/source task must repeat the direct `<cstdint>` include rule, `std::int64_t` spelling, exact IClock signature, consistent override rule, zero-third-party self-contained test-main rule, exact CMake test target, and minimal runtime entry. Relying on transitive standard-library includes is forbidden


Medium-size reference from MetaProjectDev (descriptive only; the architecture model's generated file count is authoritative):
- about 9 repository files
- about 37 functions or methods
- about 786 lines of code

Sizing guidance:
- #Files, #Functions, and #LOC above are paper-table references, not acceptance bounds
- use the number of files produced by this architecture run; do not add or remove files merely to hit the reference
- count build, runtime, test, package markers, headers, and implementation files when reporting the realized size

Required domain behavior:
- media metadata
- playlist navigation
- play pause and stop state
- seek and duration bounds
- volume and mute
- headless deterministic playback clock

Cross-cutting requirements:
- separate pure domain logic from runtime, UI, filesystem, network, clock, and randomness boundaries
- automated tests must be deterministic, headless, offline, and require no manual interaction
- keep the single test target concise (2 to 4 tests, preferably under 150 LOC): cover runtime wiring and representative core rules, not the full feature matrix
- do not inflate the function/LOC target with test code; put substantive behavior in implementation files
- make every planned file small enough for one 4096-token code completion: prefer under 150 LOC and never plan a file over 220 LOC
- order the Task list strictly by implementation dependency: foundational types and interfaces first, then dependent implementations, then the runtime entry, and the single test target LAST (the build descriptor may be first)
- the Engineer code_todos must preserve that dependency-first Task-list order so later files can see already-generated dependency code
- the runtime entry must provide a small non-interactive demonstration that exits successfully or starts safely without an output loop
- validate invalid inputs and boundary cases
- keep public interfaces coherent across design, task list, implementation, and tests
- specify one canonical public API; tests must use it without inventing alternate semantics
- make Full API spec non-empty and exhaustive: for every public type/function give its exact module, signature, return value, error behavior, and key semantics; repeat these exact contracts in each affected file task
- tests may import only the canonical public API and should assert stable externally visible behavior, not private implementation details, incidental formatting, or unplanned aliases
- avoid circular dependencies; explicitly give the allowed import/include direction and ensure every referenced symbol is defined before a dependent file is generated
- avoid network access and OS-specific behavior during build, tests, and runtime checks
- all planned source, header, build, and test files must be listed exactly and consistently in the design and task documents


FINAL NON-NEGOTIABLE VIDEO-PLAYER C++ COMPILATION CHECKLIST:
- Task filenames are exactly: CMakeLists.txt; include/Time/IClock.h; include/Time/ManualClock.h; include/Time/MonotonicClock.h; include/Media/MediaMetadata.h; include/Playlist/Playlist.h; include/Player/PlaybackState.h; include/Player/Player.h; include/Runtime/App.h; src/Time/ManualClock.cpp; src/Time/MonotonicClock.cpp; src/Media/MediaMetadata.cpp; src/Playlist/Playlist.cpp; src/Player/Player.cpp; src/Runtime/App.cpp; src/Main.cpp; tests/test_main.cpp.
- IClock.h directly contains `#include <cstdint>` and declares `virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0;`. Every header that names a signed 64-bit integer directly includes `<cstdint>`, every such type is spelled `std::int64_t`, and bare `int64_t` is forbidden.
- tests/test_main.cpp contains exactly one self-contained `int main()` and uses no GoogleTest or other test framework. CMake directly builds and registers video_player_tests without find_package, FetchContent, GTest, gtest, or any network dependency.
- src/Main.cpp only returns Runtime::App().run_demo() and never streams PlaybackState or another enum.
- Base/derived and header/source signatures use identical const and noexcept qualifiers. Do not summarize or omit these literal compilation tokens from Full API, Shared Knowledge, or affected implementation tasks.

Derived clocks override exactly that signature with identical const and noexcept in headers and sources. Derived clocks override exactly that signature with identical const and noexcept in headers and sources. every reusable module has matching include/*.h and src/*.cpp","tests/test_main.cpp must include headers only and must define exactly one int main()","Prohibit third-party testing libraries; use only C++17 standard library","Do not rely on transitive includes: each header lists its own required standard headers","Project-specific 64-bit contract: every header that names a signed 64-bit integer must directly include <cstdint> and spell the type as std::int64_t (never bare int64_t)","Time/IClock.h must begin with #include <cstdint> and declare virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0;","ManualClock and MonotonicClock override exactly std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept; keep noexcept/const consistent in headers and sources","src/Main.cpp contains only a minimal int main() that returns Runtime::App().run_demo() and has no interactive or long-running loop","CMake directly builds tests with add_executable(video_player_tests tests/test_main.cpp), links the core library, calls enable_testing(), and registers add_test without find_package or network"],"Domain Reasoning":["Playback timing is a pure-domain responsibility driven by a clock boundary; implement IClock with ManualClock (deterministic) and MonotonicClock (real-time) to separate environment from logic","Player manages state transitions: Stopped, Paused, Playing; updates position using clock deltas, clamping to media duration","Playlist provides deterministic navigation and selection among MediaMetadata entries; navigation returns success/failure without side effects beyond selection","MediaMetadata contains validated duration and descriptive fields; duration bounds checks are critical for seek and playback clamping","Volume and mute are domain properties: volume as an integer 0–100, independent mute flag; effective output can be inferred but no audio output","Seeking must clamp within [0, duration] and update last-timestamp references coherently","Runtime/App composes the clock, playlist, and player for a small deterministic demo without I/O loops or GUI","Tests must drive ManualClock to assert deterministic playback progress and rule enforcement"],"Domain Expectations":["MediaMetadata validates non-negative durations; zero-duration media is allowed but cannot advance playback","Player play() sets state to Playing only when a current media exists; pause() sets Paused; stop() sets Stopped and resets position to 0","Player seek(ms) clamps to [0, current_media_duration] and preserves state (Playing/Paused) while resetting last-tick reference","Player update_to_now() uses IClock to compute elapsed time since last tick when in Playing; advances position and clamps to duration; on reaching duration, sets state to Paused and position to duration","Player supports set_volume(int 0..100) and mute/unmute; volume clamped to bounds; mute is independent from volume level","Playlist supports add(), size(), get(index), select(index) returning bool, current_index(), next()/prev() with bounds; no wrap-around by default","Switching playlist item resets player position to 0 and sets state to Stopped; subsequent play() begins from 0","MonotonicClock reads steady time; ManualClock provides deterministic control for tests and demos"],"Product Goals":["Deliver a clean, deterministic C++17 core for a headless video player domain (no decoding) with clear separation of concerns","Provide a minimal, strictly specified build and test pipeline that is self-contained and reproducible","Ensure strong API contracts and input validation to simplify future extension and UI integration"],"User Stories":["As a user, I can load a playlist of media items and move to next/previous items deterministically","As a user, I can play, pause, and stop playback and see position bounded by each media’s duration","As a user, I can seek to a specific position within media and the player clamps to valid bounds","As a user, I can set volume and toggle mute independently of volume level","As a developer, I can run a deterministic demo and tests without external dependencies or manual steps"],"Competitive Analysis":["VLC: comprehensive media player with rich features; far beyond scope; our focus is core domain logic only","MPV: scriptable, powerful player; highlights separation of core and interfaces","ffplay (FFmpeg): minimal player; demonstrates clock-tied playback but relies on native libs","Simple educational players: often conflate UI and logic; The architecture must use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. Deterministic time must be provided via an IClock boundary with a ManualClock for tests and a MonotonicClock for runtime. The 64-bit timing contract is strict: every header that names a signed 64-bit integer directly includes <cstdint> and uses std::int64_t spelling; IClock.h must begin with <cstdint> and declare virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0; ManualClock and MonotonicClock must override exactly that signature consistently in headers and sources. Domain behavior includes media metadata (duration), playlist navigation without wrap, playback state transitions (play/pause/stop), seek and duration clamping, volume and mute handling, and a headless deterministic update path. Tests need to be concise (2–4 tests, under ~150 LOC), deterministic, and headless. The CMake test target must be built directly (no find_package), registered with add_test, and invoked via ctest. navigation returns success/failure without side effects beyond selection","MediaMetadata contains validated duration and descriptive fields; duration bounds checks are critical for seek and playback clamping","Volume and mute are domain properties: volume as an integer 0–100, independent mute flag; effective output can be inferred but no audio output","Seeking must clamp within [0, duration] and update last-timestamp references coherently","Runtime/App composes the clock, playlist, and player for a small deterministic demo without I/O loops or GUI","Tests must drive ManualClock to assert deterministic playback progress and rule enforcement"],"Domain Expectations":["MediaMetadata validates non-negative durations; zero-duration media is allowed but cannot advance playback","Player play() sets state to Playing only when a current media exists; pause() sets Paused; stop() sets Stopped and resets position to 0","Player seek(ms) clamps to [0, current_media_duration] and preserves state (Playing/Paused) while resetting last-tick reference","Player update_to_now() uses IClock to compute elapsed time since last tick when in Playing; advances position and clamps to duration; on reaching duration, sets state to Paused and position to duration","Player supports set_volume(int 0..100) and mute/unmute; volume clamped to bounds; mute is independent from volume level","Playlist supports add(), size(), get(index), select(index) returning bool, current_index(), next()/prev() with bounds; no wrap-around by default","Switching playlist item resets player position to 0 and sets state to Stopped; subsequent play() begins from 0","MonotonicClock reads steady time; ManualClock provides deterministic control for tests and demos"],"Product Goals":["Deliver a clean, deterministic C++17 core for a headless video player domain (no decoding) with clear separation of concerns","Provide a minimal, strictly specified build and test pipeline that is self-contained and reproducible","Ensure strong API contracts and input validation to simplify future extension and UI integration"],"User Stories":["As a user, I can load a playlist of media items and move to next/previous items deterministically","As a user, I can play, pause, and stop playback and see position bounded by each media’s duration","As a user, I can seek to a specific position within media and the player clamps to valid bounds","As a user, I can set volume and toggle mute independently of volume level","As a developer, I can run a deterministic demo and tests without external dependencies or manual steps"],"Competitive Analysis":["VLC: comprehensive media player with rich features; far beyond scope; our focus is core domain logic only","MPV: scriptable, powerful player; highlights separation of core and interfaces","ffplay (FFmpeg): minimal player; demonstrates clock-tied playback but relies on native libs","Simple educational players: often conflate UI and logic; our design keeps clear boundaries"],"Competitive Quadrant Chart":"quadrantChart

The architecture must use include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs for reusable modules. Deterministic time must be provided via an IClock boundary with a ManualClock for tests and a MonotonicClock for runtime. The 64-bit timing contract is strict: every header that names a signed 64-bit integer directly includes <cstdint> and uses std::int64_t spelling; IClock.h must begin with <cstdint> and declare virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0; ManualClock and MonotonicClock must override exactly that signature consistently in headers and sources. Domain behavior includes media metadata (duration), playlist navigation without wrap, playback state transitions (play/pause/stop), seek and duration clamping, volume and mute handling, and a headless deterministic update path. Tests need to be concise (2–4 tests, under ~150 LOC), deterministic, and headless. The CMake test target must be built directly (no find_package), registered with add_test, and invoked via ctest. Public API must be canonical so tests import only headers. Files should be small (ideally under 150 LOC each) and ordered by dependency to avoid circular includes.","Requirement Pool":[["P0","Preserve protocol-required files and paths exactly (CMakeLists.txt; src/Main.cpp; tests/test_main.cpp) and build via ctest"],["P0","Enforce fixed 64-bit time type rules and exact IClock signature across headers/sources"],["P0","Implement core domain behaviors: metadata, playlist navigation, playback states, seek clamping, volume/mute"],["P1","Provide ManualClock and MonotonicClock with deterministic and monotonic behavior respectively"],["P1","Deliver concise deterministic tests (2–4) covering runtime wiring and key rules"]],"UI / UX / Interaction Design draft":"Headless runtime with a tiny demo: construct a playlist, create a Player with ManualClock, perform a simple sequence (play, advance time, pause/stop), and exit. No GUI rendering or input loops. Tests avoid real rendering and manual input by using ManualClock and direct API calls.","Anything UNCLEAR":"Actual media decoding, audio/video output, and file I/O are out of scope; we focus on domain logic only. Playlist wrap-around is unspecified; we choose no wrap by default. End-of-media behavior is chosen as auto-pause at duration with position clamped; if alternative behavior (auto-stop or auto-next) is desired, it can be specified later."}

Split the domain into small C++17 modules with include/*.h and src/*.cpp pairs: time boundary (IClock, ManualClock, MonotonicClock), media metadata, playlist, player state and logic, and a tiny runtime App. Separate pure domain logic from environment: Player, Playlist, MediaMetadata are pure; ManualClock is deterministic; MonotonicClock is environment-touching but not used in tests; Main is tiny. Tests are headless and deterministic, drive ManualClock directly, and include only headers. Enforce the fixed-width integer contract strictly: each header that names a signed 64-bit integer directly includes <cstdint> and spells std::int64_t; IClock.h begins with #include <cstdint> and declares virtual std::int64_t now_ms() const noexcept = 0;. Derived clocks override exactly that signature with identical const and noexcept in headers and sources. The build uses one CMakeLists.txt: build a core library from all src/*.cpp except src/Main.cpp; link a demo executable and a single self-contained test executable; enable_testing() and
